There is a story that is told from time to time. Often late at night. Sometimes amid harsh laughter around tables laden with beer pitchers and peanuts. Sometimes as a semi serious retort in online communities. When it is told the response ranges from curiosity to disbelief. It symbolizes the foolishness of love and the redeeming gift of patience and the folly of mortal men striving to bring order to chaos.

It is a brief story, as stories such as this tend to be. With more untold than told. Such that the reader or listener's imagination fills in the wanted details through the lenses of their own experiences. And those details vary widely and wildly. As they must, given the matter at hand.

And the story at last is simply this: That once there lived a man who loved his girlfriend so much that he digitized all (were there really so many?) six seasons of The Nanny. And placed them on their shared media server. So that they could be...watched.
